messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: I face errors when comparing two models(Error in solve.default(A %*% P.inv %*% t(A)).
parts:
It's hard to tell exactly what you are trying to model.  Are Y1/Y2/Y3 indicators of a latent construct, measured at 3 occasions (pre, mid, and post)?  If so, you should be measuring common factors of items within the same occasion, not common variance of a single item across occasions.

teach.pre =~ a*Y1.pre + b*Y2.pre + c*Y3.pre
teach.mid =~ a*Y1.mid + b*Y2.mid + c*Y3.mid
teach.post =~ a*Y1.post + b*Y2.post + c*Y3.post
teach_i =~ 1*teach.pre + 1*teach.mid + 1*teach.post
teach_s =~ 0*teach.pre + 1*teach.mid + 2*teach.post

Instead, what you currently have are constructs for common variance within an item, but across occasions:
# effect of teach on attitude
# Y1/Y2/Y3.teach
Y1.teach =~ Y1.pre + a*Y1.mid + b*Y1.post
Y2.teach =~ Y2.pre + a*Y2.mid + b*Y2.post
Y3.teach =~ Y3.pre + a*Y3.mid + b*Y3.post
# intercepts & slopes of teach
teach_i =~ 1*Y1.teach + 1*Y2.teach + 1*Y3.teach
teach_s =~ 0*Y1.teach + 1*Y2.teach + 2*Y3.teach
What mistake did I make? How could I fix the problem?

I'm not sure exactly what caused the specific error you saw, but if it persists after you change your syntax above, you should post your full R syntax (not just lavaan model syntax) and some data, so that the problem can be reproduced.

You can read more about growth curve models for latent variables in this short text:

http://www.sagepub.com/textbooks/Book229205
In addition, I'd like know how to constrain covariances among errors/residuals of each time point observation.

You constrain them with labels, the same way you did to constrain intercepts in your model syntax.  (co)variance parameters are specified with the "~~" operator, as you can see in my response to your other post this evening, and in the help page for lavaan syntax:

?lavaanify # type this into your R console

as well as on the lavaan tutorial web pages:

http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/syntax2.html

Terry

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: I face errors when comparing two models(Error in solve.default(A %*% P.inv %*% t(A)).
parts:
On 04/28/2015 01:31 AM, Galaxy Brown wrote:
>>lavTestLRT(fit.model.teach.att, fit.model.teach.att1)
> Error in solve.default(A %*% P.inv %*% t(A)) :

This may be a bug in 0.5-18. I have seen it before, only in the
categorical case. A workaround is to use:

lavTestLRT(fit.model.teach.att, fit.model.teach.att1,
method="Satorra.Bentler.2010")

which gives you a mean-adjusted only difference test, but it will be in
the ballpark.

Yves.

Dear Yves,
 
This message is just for your reference in case you investigate the issue at some point. I have faced a similar problem when testing for measurement invariance for all loadings and thresholds in a two-group analysis of real (not simulated) data. The error message  I got for the PML estimator is
 
Error in solve.default(MinvHtM) :
  Lapack routine dgesv: system is exactly singular: U[9,9] = 0

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: I face errors when comparing two models(Error in solve.default(A %*% P.inv %*% t(A)).
parts: > Error in solve.default(A %*% P.inv %*% t(A)) :

This error is due to a bug in 0.5-18 that appears if two (nested) models
are compared using method = "satorra.2000", and either 1) the order of
the free parameters is different in the two models, or 2) one of the two
models contains equality constraints.

I think I have fixed this now in dev 0.5-19.850, but further testing is
needed. To download/install this version, see:

http://lavaan.ugent.be/development.html

Yves.

parts:
The example Benny posted appears to work ok now. I have another one where a similar problem is showing up when using "satorra.2000". I'm using lavaan version 0.5-20, and just happen to be experimenting with fitting models common in behavioral genetics so the data and some of the code comes from OpenMx: http://openmx.psyc.virginia.edu/docs/OpenMx/latest/GeneticEpi_Path.html

library(OpenMx)
library(lavaan)

data(twinData)

# Select Variables for Analysis
## Note that this appears to just grab data for females
selVars   <- c('bmi1','bmi2')
aceVars   <- c("A1","C1","E1","A2","C2","E2")

# Select Data for Analysis
mzData    <- subset(twinData, zyg==1, selVars)
dzData    <- subset(twinData, zyg==3, selVars)
mzData<-cbind(mzData, 1)
dzData<-cbind(dzData, .5)
colnames(mzData)<-c("bmi1","bmi2","R")
colnames(dzData)<-c("bmi1","bmi2","R")
dat<-rbind(mzData,dzData)
dat.narm<-na.omit(dat) ## removes cases w/ missing values

## Unconstrained model
myModel<-"
E1 =~ c(e,e)*bmi1 + start(.5)*bmi1
C1 =~ c(c,c)*bmi1 + start(.5)*bmi1
A1 =~ c(a,a)*bmi1 + start(.5)*bmi1
A2 =~ c(a,a)*bmi2 + start(.5)*bmi2
C2 =~ c(c,c)*bmi2 + start(.5)*bmi2
E2 =~ c(e,e)*bmi2 + start(.5)*bmi2

E1 ~~ 1*E1
C1 ~~ 1*C1
A1 ~~ 1*A1
E2 ~~ 1*E2
C2 ~~ 1*C2
A2 ~~ 1*A2

E1 ~~ 0*E2
C1 ~~ 1*C2
A1 ~~ c(1,.5)*A2

bmi1 ~ c(int,int)*1
bmi2 ~ c(int,int)*1
"
modr<-lavaan(model = myModel, data=dat.narm, group="R", estimator="MLM",mimic="EQS")

## Constrained model
myModel2<-"
E1 =~ c(e,e)*bmi1 + start(.5)*bmi1
C1 =~ c(c,c)*bmi1 + 0*bmi1
A1 =~ c(a,a)*bmi1 + start(.5)*bmi1
A2 =~ c(a,a)*bmi2 + start(.5)*bmi2
C2 =~ c(c,c)*bmi2 + 0*bmi2
E2 =~ c(e,e)*bmi2 + start(.5)*bmi2

E1 ~~ 1*E1
C1 ~~ 1*C1
A1 ~~ 1*A1
E2 ~~ 1*E2
C2 ~~ 1*C2
A2 ~~ 1*A2

E1 ~~ 0*E2
C1 ~~ 1*C2
A1 ~~ c(1,.5)*A2

bmi1 ~ c(int,int)*1
bmi2 ~ c(int,int)*1
"
modr2<-lavaan(model = myModel2, data=dat.narm, group="R", estimator="MLM",mimic="EQS")

## Fails, with error:
## Error in solve.default(A %*% P.inv %*% t(A)) : 'a' is 0-diml
lavTestLRT(modr,modr2, method="satorra.2000")

## Works
lavTestLRT(modr,modr2, method="satorra.bentler.2010")
